rationale: The measured unit is one complete batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward; the independently measured baseline is latency_ms=4.237417 (project.json original_baseline; current revision f2cfe831 has no accepted bundles installed). execution_timeline-1221e205 shows 88 kernels with kernel_active_union_us=4066.6 vs gaps_between_kernels_us=81.1 over a 4147.7us span on a single serial stream (compute_overlap_us=0.0): the invocation is GPU-compute-bound, so only removing GPU kernel time moves latency_ms materially (host/launch-side ceiling ~2%). Leaf-family diagnostics: aten::conv2d 3043.1us (20 calls), aten::batch_norm 428.5us (20 calls), aten::relu 341.9us (17), max_pool2d 200.1us, add_ 121.0us. All 20 batch_norm kernels sit directly after a bias-free conv2d (observed conv2d signatures have bias=None) inside a ResNetConvLayer (17 calls: embedder stem + 16 stage convs) or ResNetShortCut (3 calls) running with training=False and frozen running stats (observed batch_norm signatures), so every site admits the exact inference fold scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), W'=W*scale, b'=beta-scale*mean. Selecting all 20 module calls as one joint bundle keeps the strategy coherent (partial folding would mix eager BN with folded sites) and every edit is a direct module callable boundary under the legacy binding backend that explicitly replaces the conv+BN bundle, so no inherited required call inside those bundles is left dangling; the unchanged aten::relu/max_pool2d/add_ work continues to execute in the surviving parents. Lazy one-time folding at first invocation is legitimate setup per the binding contract and lands in quality/warmup (warmup=2 precede repeats=5), outside timed repeats. Precision policy is untouched (FP32 fold arithmetic only; TF32 off, no autocast/quantization, cudnn.benchmark unchanged); cost is one folded parameter copy ~45MB, which peak_allocated_bytes reports but no constraint binds to latency_ms for this request.
hypothesis: Replacing forward of all 17 ResNetConvLayer calls (groups 836e80426d566f8f5dce, 0022893ec8c1ceea869f, 39b672d8d4bea8959c44, 867f8d20e37fedce71c4, c30ffc96e594cd4d7734) and all 3 ResNetShortCut calls (groups 04fe5ffd91a3ecdc1ced, 9c1e6f2c47a84d7de11d, 4e7e7ecf95e285fe008e) with a lazily-cached BN-folded F.conv2d(x, W', b') followed by the unchanged activation eliminates all 20 aten::batch_norm kernels, i.e. 428.5us of serial GPU leaf time (10.5% of the 4066.6us busy union), while conv kernels keep their time up to a negligible bias epilogue; expected latency_ms drops from ~4.24 to ~3.8 (-8..11%) and images_per_second (exact reciprocal at fixed batch) rises proportionally, keeping the 0.95 memory-goal throughput ratio. Numerical fidelity was pre-validated on the worker CPU python (transformers 5.16.1, torch 2.13.0) with the exact frozen weights and exact batch=32 workload input: folding all 20 sites reproduces the full 1000-class logits with max_abs_err=7.6e-6, 0/32000 violations of atol+rtol*|ref| (atol=rtol=1e-4), exact top-1 preserved (min reference top1-top2 margin 0.1446, four orders of magnitude above the observed error), and the warm cached path is bit-stable across repeated invocations. This remains a hypothesis until the framework's independent GPU validation confirms the quality checks and the wall-latency reduction; if GPU conv timing shifts under folded weights or the bias epilogue costs more than expected, realized benefit will be smaller than the removed BN leaf time, and follow-up elementwise opportunities (exact relu-maxpool fusion in the stem, add-relu fusion in ResNetBasicLayer) remain available as separate candidates.
